workflow.name: Asset Hawk – Data Room Occupancy Check

summary.answer: No. Across the data room, V7 Go extracted a seller-claimed occupancy of 95% vs 73% observed from orbital parked-car counts (71–75% range; 34 cars over 48 dwellings, 0.71 cars/dwelling, stable across loops). That is a 22-point material overstatement: ~27% physical vacancy vs 5% claimed, the £3.42m TTM rent is unsupported, and the Underwriting Memo puts unsupported value at £10–13m (in-place income ~-23%). Recommendation: bid off 73% with a 150 bps vacancy reserve.
summary.note: Summary composed from the five V7 Go row outputs (4 of 5 documents flagged 'Material overstatement'; the Site Imagery Pack has no figures and is 'Insufficient data').

documents.underwriting_finding: According to the Occupancy Analysis Report, the seller's claimed occupancy of 95% is materially overstated by 22 percentage points compared to the observed orbital occupancy of 73% (71–75% range). Satellite observation identified a median of 34 parked cars across 48 counted dwellings, reflecting 0.71 cars per dwelling and a 34/48 car-at-kerb occupancy driven down by the West terrace (67%) and South car park (71%) tiles. Because parked-car detections remained stable across nadir loops, the data reflects structural vacancy rather than day-to-day variance, confirming a material overstatement of the rent roll that impacts underwriting valuation.

documents.underwriting_finding: The seller's claimed occupancy of 95% is materially overstated by 22 percentage points compared to the observed occupancy of 73%. According to the "Vehicle Count Time Series," the property recorded a stable median of 34 regional parked cars (with 3 through-traffic vehicles excluded), remaining consistently below the baseline of 0.7–0.9 cars per occupied unit expected for a 95% occupied 142-unit block. This document provides vital supporting evidence by establishing temporal stability in vehicle counts, verifying that transient traffic or one-off deliveries do not account for the 22-point occupancy deficit.

documents.underwriting_finding: As flagged by the insufficient data status, the Site Imagery Pack does not provide numerical figures for seller-claimed or observed occupancy, precluding a determination of whether occupancy is overstated or by how many percentage points. Instead, the document provides supporting methodological evidence by capturing four tasked nadir tiles—Tile Z-N North courtyard, Tile Z-E East street grid, Tile Z-W West terrace, and Tile Z-S South car park—independent of the seller's data room. It contributes to the occupancy case by establishing VLM overlay tracking for house footprints (gold), cars (cyan), and people (signal red) per frame with interpolation to support forthcoming orbital vehicle and activity counts.
